chunks: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:

If you finish part of your wudu (ablution) and the water runs out before you complete it, then when water is brought, complete your wudu if what you had washed is still moist. But if it has dried, then repeat your wudu. And if some of your wudu dries before you complete the wudu, without the water being cut off from you, then wash what remains, whether your wudu has dried or has not dried.

key_terms.جَفَّ: dried, referring to the loss of moisture on washed limbs
key_terms.رَطْبًا: still moist, indicating the earlier washed parts have not dried
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ: then repeat, meaning to begin the wudu again
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْ: then wash, meaning to continue with the remaining parts
key_terms.وُضُوئِكَ: your wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if parts of wudu dry before the ablution is completed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on continuity in wudu (ablution). If water becomes unavailable and the previously washed parts dry, the wudu must be restarted; but if water remains available, one may continue washing the remaining parts even if some earlier parts have dried.
